title: Making a simple timber bird box
subtitle: Cut and assemble a nest box from untreated rough-sawn softwood for common garden birds
excerpt: How to make a simple wooden bird box from rough-sawn softwood. Covers cutting the six pieces, drilling the entrance hole, assembling with exterior wood glue and screws, fitting a hinged roof for cleaning, and siting the finished box.
sourceNotes: RSPB bird box guidance (open access). Traditional nest box construction practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: The diameter of the circular entrance hole determines which species will use the box. The RSPB recommended sizes are: 25 mm for blue tit, 28 mm for great tit, 32 mm for house sparrow and nuthatch, 45 mm for starling. Cutting the hole smaller than 25 mm will exclude most small birds entirely.

content.text: A bird box is a six-piece box from rough-sawn softwood, assembled with exterior glue and screws and fitted with a hinged roof for annual cleaning. The
is the critical dimension: it determines which species will nest.

attrs.title: Timber choice
attrs.body: Use rough-sawn (not planed) softwood 15 to 20 mm thick. The rough surface gives birds grip on the interior walls. Do not use treated timber or preservative inside a nest box; the chemicals can harm nestlings.

content.text: The standard small-bird box dimensions are: front panel 200 x 150 mm; back panel 300 x 150 mm (the extra 100 mm at the bottom is the fixing flap for attaching to a tree or post); two side panels cut with the top edge angled at 10 to 15 degrees so the roof drains forward; a floor panel 100 x 100 mm; and a roof panel 200 x 175 mm with a slight overhang at the front. Adjust all dimensions proportionally for larger-species boxes.
Drill the entrance hole and drainage holes

Drill the entrance hole in the front panel with a Forstner or spade bit at the correct diameter for the target species (25 mm for blue tit, 32 mm for house sparrow). Centre the hole 125 mm from the bottom of the front panel. Drill three or four 6 mm drainage holes in the floor panel to prevent water pooling inside.

Assemble the front, back, and two side panels first with an exterior PVA wood glue and 40 mm screws. Screw the floor panel in from underneath. Do not glue or permanently fix the roof: hinge it with a short strip of rubber (a piece of bicycle inner tube or a roofing membrane offcut) or fit a small piano hinge so the roof can be lifted for cleaning. The roof must overlap the front and sides by at least 30 mm to keep rain out.

Leave the box untreated; bare weathered wood is what birds prefer. Fix the box using the back flap to a tree trunk or fence post 2 to 4 metres above the ground, facing somewhere between north and south-east to avoid direct afternoon sun and prevailing rain. Clean the box in late summer each year (after the birds have left) by removing old nest material and scalding the inside with boiling water.

attrs.symptom: Box remains unused after several seasons
attrs.cause: Sited in too exposed or disturbed a location, facing the wrong direction, or entrance hole wrong for local species.
attrs.fix: Move the box to a less disturbed position with more shelter from the prevailing wind. Check which species are present in the garden and adjust the entrance hole diameter to match.

attrs.symptom: Box filling with water in heavy rain
attrs.cause: Drainage holes blocked or absent, or roof does not overhang enough.
attrs.fix: Clear the drainage holes in the floor and ensure the roof overhang is at least 30 mm at the front.
